goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

goldens.comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

candidates: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 - OptimizedCursorPaginator handles the datetime key as a number, so the optimized path crashes. The audit log endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a datetime raise `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key` on the results, so every optimized request that returns any rows fails with a 500. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value, which `build_queryset` then compares against a datetime column, giving wrong filtering or errors on later pages. Fix: subclass `DateTimePaginator`, or reuse its `get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor`, which convert between epoch milliseconds and datetime.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 - `organization_context.member` can be None, so every audit-log request can crash. This line runs on every request, not only when `optimized_pagination=true` is set. When the caller is not a superuser and the org context has no member, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500. That happens for org-level API key or token auth, and for staff who are not members. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is Optional; I could not see whether `OrganizationAuditPermission` lets these callers through. It also checks the raw `request.user.is_superuser` flag instead of `is_active_superuser(request)`, so a user with the flag but no active superuser session still gets the privileged path. Fix: compute this only inside the `use_optimized` branch, use `is_active_superuser(request)`, and guard against `member is None`.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 - Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing raise instead of paginating. Django querysets do not support negative indexing. A client-supplied cursor with a negative offset (for example `cursor=0:-10:0`) makes `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, so the request returns a 500 instead of a page. The `is_prev` branch at line 884 passes a negative offset through unchanged in the same way. The comments saying the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" and that this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" are wrong. Fix: clamp to `max(0, cursor.offset)` in every branch, or reject cursors with a negative offset.
